name: featureflags
description: Feature flags: targeting rules, segments, prerequisites, stable percentage rollouts, OpenFeature-style details, JSON definitions and a SQLite store with audit

api.name: FlagValue
api.sig: pub type FlagValue = BoolV{v: Bool} | StrV{v: Str} | IntV{v: Int} | NumV{v: F64} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The value of one variant.

api.name: type_name
api.sig: fn type_name(v: FlagValue) -> Str
api.doc: The name of a value's type: `boolean`, `string`, `integer` or `number`.

api.name: Context
api.sig: pub type Context = {key: Str, attrs: Map[Str, Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Who a flag is evaluated for: the targeting key (a user, account or device id; used for
explicit targets and as the default bucketing key) and string attributes. A rule's attribute
`key` means the targeting key unless the attributes define `key` themselves.

api.name: context
api.sig: fn context(key: Str) -> Context
api.doc: A context for `key` with no attributes.

api.name: with_attr
api.sig: fn with_attr(c: Context, name: Str, value: Str) -> Context
api.doc: The context with attribute `name` set to `value`.

api.name: attr
api.sig: fn attr(c: Context, name: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The value of attribute `name` in `c`, or none. `key` falls back to the targeting key, and an
empty targeting key counts as missing.

api.name: Op
api.sig: pub type Op = Equals | NotEquals | In | NotIn | Contains | NotContains | StartsWith | EndsWith | Lt | Le | Gt | Ge | Matches | Before | After | Exists | NotExists derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A comparison in a rule. Every operator except `NotExists` is false when the attribute is
missing. `Equals` and `NotEquals` take one value, `In` and `NotIn` one or more, the string
operators (`Contains`, `NotContains`, `StartsWith`, `EndsWith`) and `Matches` (a regular
expression; the stdlib engine runs in linear time, so a pattern can't hang the server) are true
when any value fits, `Lt` `Le` `Gt` `Ge` compare numbers (false if either side isn't one),
`Before` and `After` compare ISO 8601 times, and `Exists` and `NotExists` take no values.
Comparisons are exact and case-sensitive.

api.name: Clause
api.sig: pub type Clause = AttrClause{attr: Str, op: Op, values: List[Str]} | SegmentClause{segment: Str} | AllClauses{cs: List[Clause]} | AnyClause{cs: List[Clause]} | NotClause{c: Clause} | AlwaysClause derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A targeting condition: an attribute comparison, membership of a segment, or a combination.
`AllClauses([])` is true and `AnyClause([])` is false.

api.name: Serve
api.sig: pub type Serve = Fixed{variant: Str} | Weighted{weights: List[(Str, Int)], bucket_by: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What a rule (or the fallthrough) serves: one variant, or a weighted split of variants by a
stable hash of the bucketing attribute (`bucket_by`, `key` for the targeting key). Weights are
relative non-negative integers (percentages, or parts of 100000 for finer steps).

api.name: Rule
api.sig: pub type Rule = {id: Str, when: Clause, serve: Serve} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A targeting rule: when `when` holds, serve `serve`. `id` names it in evaluation details.

api.name: Target
api.sig: pub type Target = {variant: Str, keys: List[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: Contexts whose targeting key is in `keys` get `variant`, before any rule: allow and deny lists.

api.name: Prereq
api.sig: pub type Prereq = {flag: Str, variants: List[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The flag `flag` must evaluate to one of `variants` for this flag to be on.

api.name: Flag
api.sig: pub type Flag = {key: Str, enabled: Bool, variants: List[(Str, FlagValue)], off_variant: Str, fallthrough: Serve, targets: List[Target], rules: List[Rule], prerequisites: List[Prereq], salt: Str, version: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A flag. When `enabled` is false it serves `off_variant`. Otherwise its prerequisites must hold
(else `off_variant`), then explicit targets, then the first matching rule, then `fallthrough`
decide. `salt` changes every bucket of the flag at once (leave it `""` to bucket by the key
alone); `version` counts changes.

api.name: Segment
api.sig: pub type Segment = {key: Str, included: List[Str], excluded: List[Str], rules: List[Clause]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A reusable set of contexts: `excluded` keys never belong, `included` keys always do, and
otherwise a context belongs when any of `rules` holds. Segment rules may not refer to segments.

api.name: Snapshot
api.sig: pub type Snapshot = {flags: Map[Str, Flag], segments: Map[Str, Segment], version: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A set of flags and segments, with the version of the store they came from (0 for a file).
Share it between request handlers as any immutable value.

api.name: bool_flag
api.sig: fn bool_flag(key: Str, enabled: Bool) -> Flag
api.doc:
A boolean flag: `on` (true) and `off` (false), off when disabled, on for everyone when enabled
unless rules say otherwise.

api.name: string_flag
api.sig: fn string_flag(key: Str, enabled: Bool, variants: List[(Str, Str)], default_variant: Str, off_variant: Str) -> Flag
api.doc:
A flag with string variants, serving `default_variant` to everyone when enabled and
`off_variant` when disabled.

api.name: add_rule
api.sig: fn add_rule(f: Flag, rule: Rule) -> Flag
api.doc: The flag with `rule` added after its other rules.

api.name: add_target
api.sig: fn add_target(f: Flag, variant: Str, keys: List[Str]) -> Flag
api.doc: The flag with an explicit target: `keys` get `variant`.

api.name: add_prereq
api.sig: fn add_prereq(f: Flag, flag: Str, variants: List[Str]) -> Flag
api.doc: The flag with a prerequisite.

api.name: with_fallthrough
api.sig: fn with_fallthrough(f: Flag, s: Serve) -> Flag
api.doc: The flag serving `s` when no target or rule decides.

api.name: rollout
api.sig: fn rollout(on: Str, off: Str, pct: F64 where _ >= 0.0 and _ <= 100.0) -> Serve
api.doc:
A percentage rollout: `pct` percent (0 to 100, in steps of 0.001) of contexts, by targeting key,
get `on`, the rest `off`. Raising the percentage later keeps everyone who already had `on`.

api.name: rule
api.sig: fn rule(id: Str, attr: Str, op: Op, values: List[Str], serve: Serve) -> Rule
api.doc: A rule matching one attribute.

api.name: snapshot
api.sig: fn snapshot(flags: List[Flag], segments: List[Segment]) -> Snapshot
api.doc: A snapshot of these flags and segments (later ones replace earlier ones with the same key).

api.name: bucket
api.sig: fn bucket(flag_key: Str, salt: Str, bucket_key: Str) -> Int
api.doc:
The bucket of `bucket_key` for a flag, from 0 to 99999: the first four bytes of
SHA-256(`flag_key` "." `salt` "." `bucket_key`), as an unsigned big-endian integer, scaled to
100000. The same inputs always give the same bucket, in every process and tier, and buckets are
uniform to within 0.003%.

api.name: split_variant
api.sig: fn split_variant(weights: List[(Str, Int)], b: Int where _ >= 0 and _ < 100000) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The variant a split gives to bucket `b` (0 to 99999): weights are laid out in order over the
buckets, in proportion. None when every weight is 0.

api.name: Reason
api.sig: pub type Reason = Static | Default | TargetingMatch | Split | Disabled | PrerequisiteFailed | ErrorReason derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Why a flag has the value it has, as in OpenFeature: `Static` (the flag has no targets or rules),
`Default` (nothing matched; the fallthrough variant), `TargetingMatch` (a target or rule
matched), `Split` (a weighted split chose), `Disabled` (the flag is off), `PrerequisiteFailed`
(a prerequisite did not hold; the off variant), or `ErrorReason` (see the error code; the
caller's default is used).

api.name: reason_name
api.sig: fn reason_name(r: Reason) -> Str
api.doc:
The OpenFeature spelling of a reason: `STATIC`, `DEFAULT`, `TARGETING_MATCH`, `SPLIT`,
`DISABLED`, `PREREQUISITE_FAILED` or `ERROR`.

api.name: ErrorCode
api.sig: pub type ErrorCode = FlagNotFound | TypeMismatch | ParseError | TargetingKeyMissing | InvalidContext | General derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What went wrong, as in OpenFeature: no such flag, a typed accessor for another type, a split
without its bucketing attribute, or a definition that refers to something missing or forms a
prerequisite cycle (`General`, with a message). `ParseError` and `InvalidContext` complete the
OpenFeature set for code that wraps this package (definitions that failed to load, a context
it rejects); evaluation itself never produces them.

api.name: error_name
api.sig: fn error_name(e: ErrorCode) -> Str
api.doc:
The OpenFeature spelling of an error code: `FLAG_NOT_FOUND`, `TYPE_MISMATCH`, `PARSE_ERROR`,
`TARGETING_KEY_MISSING`, `INVALID_CONTEXT` or `GENERAL`.

api.name: Details
api.sig: pub type Details = {key: Str, value: Opt[FlagValue], variant: Opt[Str], reason: Reason, error: Opt[ErrorCode], message: Str, rule: Opt[Str], flag_version: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The result of evaluating a flag: the value and variant (none on an error), why, the error code
and a message on an error, the id of the rule that matched (`target:VARIANT` for an explicit
target), and the flag's version.

api.name: clause_holds
api.sig: fn clause_holds(s: Snapshot, c: Clause, ctx: Context) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `c` holds for `ctx`, with the snapshot's segments. A clause naming a missing segment is
false (validation reports it).

api.name: in_segment
api.sig: fn in_segment(s: Snapshot, seg: Segment, ctx: Context) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `ctx` belongs to segment `seg`: not excluded, and included or matched by a rule. A
segment rule that names a segment is false (validation reports it).

api.name: evaluate
api.sig: fn evaluate(s: Snapshot, key: Str, ctx: Context) -> Details
api.doc:
Evaluates flag `key` for `ctx`. Pure: the same snapshot and context always give the same
details.

api.name: Resolved
api.sig: pub type Resolved[T] = {value: T, details: Details} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A typed result: the value (the caller's default on any error) and the details.

api.name: bool_details
api.sig: fn bool_details(s: Snapshot, key: Str, ctx: Context, default: Bool) -> Resolved[Bool]
api.doc: A boolean flag's value and details; `default` on any error, including `TypeMismatch`.

api.name: str_details
api.sig: fn str_details(s: Snapshot, key: Str, ctx: Context, default: Str) -> Resolved[Str]
api.doc: A string flag's value and details; `default` on any error.

api.name: int_details
api.sig: fn int_details(s: Snapshot, key: Str, ctx: Context, default: Int) -> Resolved[Int]
api.doc: An integer flag's value and details; `default` on any error.

api.name: num_details
api.sig: fn num_details(s: Snapshot, key: Str, ctx: Context, default: F64) -> Resolved[F64]
api.doc:
A number flag's value and details (integer variants are accepted as numbers); `default` on any
error.

api.name: is_on
api.sig: fn is_on(s: Snapshot, key: Str, ctx: Context, default: Bool) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether boolean flag `key` is on for `ctx`; `default` on any error.

api.name: str_value
api.sig: fn str_value(s: Snapshot, key: Str, ctx: Context, default: Str) -> Str
api.doc: A string flag's value for `ctx`; `default` on any error.

api.name: int_value
api.sig: fn int_value(s: Snapshot, key: Str, ctx: Context, default: Int) -> Int
api.doc: An integer flag's value for `ctx`; `default` on any error.

api.name: num_value
api.sig: fn num_value(s: Snapshot, key: Str, ctx: Context, default: F64) -> F64
api.doc: A number flag's value for `ctx`; `default` on any error.

api.name: evaluate_all
api.sig: fn evaluate_all(s: Snapshot, ctx: Context) -> List[Details]
api.doc:
Every flag of the snapshot evaluated for `ctx`, in key order: what a client-side SDK
bootstrap needs.

api.name: problems
api.sig: fn problems(s: Snapshot) -> List[Str]
api.doc:
Every problem in a snapshot, each with its path (`flags.KEY.rules[0].when.values: ...`):
unknown variants, segments and prerequisite flags, prerequisite cycles, operator arities, numbers
and times that don't parse, bad regular expressions, splits without positive weights, variants
of mixed types, duplicate names and keys that aren't allowed. Empty when the snapshot is valid.

api.name: VariantJson
api.sig: pub type VariantJson = {name: Str, boolean: Opt[Bool], string: Opt[Str], integer: Opt[Int], number: Opt[F64]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A variant on the wire: its name and exactly one of `boolean`, `string`, `integer`, `number`.

api.name: ClauseJson
api.sig: pub type ClauseJson = {attr: Opt[Str], op: Opt[Str], values: Opt[List[Str]], segment: Opt[Str], all: Opt[List[ClauseJson]], any: Opt[List[ClauseJson]], negate: Opt[ClauseJson], always: Opt[Bool]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A clause on the wire: exactly one of an attribute comparison (`attr`, `op`, `values`), `segment`,
`all`, `any` or `negate`; `{}` with `always: true` always holds.

api.name: WeightJson
api.sig: pub type WeightJson = {variant: Str, weight: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A weighted variant of a split on the wire.

api.name: ServeJson
api.sig: pub type ServeJson = {variant: Opt[Str], split: Opt[List[WeightJson]], bucket_by: Opt[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A serve on the wire: `variant`, or `split` (with an optional `bucket_by`, default `key`).

api.name: RuleJson
api.sig: pub type RuleJson = {id: Str, when: ClauseJson, serve: ServeJson} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A rule on the wire.

api.name: FlagJson
api.sig: pub type FlagJson = {key: Str, enabled: Opt[Bool], variants: List[VariantJson], off_variant: Str, fallthrough: ServeJson, targets: Opt[List[Target]], rules: Opt[List[RuleJson]], prerequisites: Opt[List[Prereq]], salt: Opt[Str], version: Opt[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A flag on the wire. Missing `targets`, `rules`, `prerequisites`, `salt` and `version` are empty
(0); a missing `enabled` is true.

api.name: SegmentJson
api.sig: pub type SegmentJson = {key: Str, included: Opt[List[Str]], excluded: Opt[List[Str]], rules: Opt[List[ClauseJson]]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A segment on the wire.

api.name: DefinitionsJson
api.sig: pub type DefinitionsJson = {flags: List[FlagJson], segments: Opt[List[SegmentJson]]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A definitions document: `{"flags": [...], "segments": [...]}`.

api.name: op_name
api.sig: fn op_name(op: Op) -> Str
api.doc: The name of an operator in the JSON format (`equals`, `not_in`, `starts_with`, `lt`, ...).

api.name: parse_op
api.sig: fn parse_op(name: Str) -> Opt[Op]
api.doc: The operator with this JSON name.

api.name: decode
api.sig: fn decode(text: Str) -> Res[Snapshot, Str]
api.doc:
The snapshot a definitions document describes, validated (see `problems`). Errors name the
path: `flags[1].rules[0].when.op: unknown operator 'eqals'`. Flags and segments must have unique
keys.

api.name: encode
api.sig: fn encode(s: Snapshot) -> Str
api.doc:
The definitions document of a snapshot; `decode` reads it back to the same flags and
segments.

api.name: encode_flag
api.sig: fn encode_flag(f: Flag) -> Str
api.doc: One flag as JSON in the definitions format.

api.name: encode_segment
api.sig: fn encode_segment(s: Segment) -> Str
api.doc: One segment as JSON in the definitions format.

api.name: decode_flag
api.sig: fn decode_flag(text: Str) -> Res[Flag, Str]
api.doc:
A flag from its JSON (one element of `flags`), checked on its own: references to other flags
and segments are checked when it joins a snapshot.

api.name: decode_segment
api.sig: fn decode_segment(text: Str) -> Res[Segment, Str]
api.doc: A segment from its JSON (one element of `segments`).

api.name: load_file
api.sig: fn load_file(path: Str) -> Res[Snapshot, Str] ! fs
api.doc: The definitions in a JSON file, validated.

api.name: fingerprint
api.sig: fn fingerprint(s: Snapshot) -> Str
api.doc:
A fingerprint of a snapshot's definitions (the SHA-256 of their JSON, in hex): equal snapshots
have equal fingerprints, so a poller can tell whether anything changed.

api.name: StoreErr
api.sig: pub type StoreErr = Invalid{msg: Str} | Conflict{key: Str, expected: Int, actual: Int} | NotFound{key: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Why a store change was refused: the change would make the definitions invalid, the flag or
segment changed since the version the caller read (`expected`), or it does not exist. The
variant names answer 400, 409 and 404 when an `http.serve` handler raises them.

api.name: AuditEntry
api.sig: pub type AuditEntry = {id: Int, kind: Str, key: Str, action: Str, definition: Opt[Str], version: Int, actor: Str, at: Time} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
One entry of the audit history: what changed (`flag` or `segment`, its key), the action (`put`
or `delete`), the definition after a put, the store version it produced, who did it and when.

api.name: open_store
api.sig: fn open_store(c: Db) -> Unit ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Creates the store's tables if they are missing (`featureflags_flags`, `featureflags_segments`,
`featureflags_audit`, `featureflags_meta`). Safe to call on every start.

api.name: store_version
api.sig: fn store_version(c: Db) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
The store's version: it increases by one with every change, so comparing it with a snapshot's
`version` is the cheap way to tell whether to reload.

api.name: load_store
api.sig: fn load_store(c: Db) -> Snapshot ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[StoreErr]
api.doc:
Every flag and segment in the store, as a snapshot with the store's version. Read in one
transaction, so it is consistent.

api.name: reload_if_changed
api.sig: fn reload_if_changed(c: Db, have: Int) -> Opt[Snapshot] ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[StoreErr]
api.doc:
The store's snapshot if its version differs from `have`, else none: a poll costs one indexed
read when nothing changed.

api.name: put_flag
api.sig: fn put_flag(c: Db, f: Flag, expected: Opt[Int], actor: Str, at: Time) -> Flag ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[StoreErr]
api.doc:
Creates or replaces flag `f`, in a transaction: the whole store must stay valid with it. With
`expected` (the flag's version the caller read, 0 for a new flag) a concurrent change is a
`Conflict` instead of being overwritten. Returns the flag as stored, with its new version.

api.name: delete_flag
api.sig: fn delete_flag(c: Db, key: Str, expected: Opt[Int], actor: Str, at: Time) -> Unit ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[StoreErr]
api.doc: Deletes flag `key`; refused while another flag has it as a prerequisite.

api.name: put_segment
api.sig: fn put_segment(c: Db, g: Segment, expected: Opt[Int], actor: Str, at: Time) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[StoreErr]
api.doc: Creates or replaces segment `g`; the store must stay valid with it.

api.name: delete_segment
api.sig: fn delete_segment(c: Db, key: Str, expected: Opt[Int], actor: Str, at: Time) -> Unit ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[StoreErr]
api.doc: Deletes segment `key`; refused while a flag uses it.

api.name: import_snapshot
api.sig: fn import_snapshot(c: Db, s: Snapshot, actor: Str, at: Time) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[StoreErr]
api.doc:
Replaces everything in the store with the snapshot's flags and segments (keeping each flag's
version counting), in one transaction, with one audit entry per change. Returns the new store
version.

api.name: history
api.sig: fn history(c: Db, kind: Str, key: Str) -> List[AuditEntry] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: The audit history of one flag or segment (`kind` is `flag` or `segment`), oldest first.

api.name: changes_since
api.sig: fn changes_since(c: Db, since: Int) -> List[AuditEntry] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: The audit entries after store version `since`, oldest first: what changed since a snapshot.

api.name: evaluate_stored
api.sig: fn evaluate_stored(c: Db, key: Str, ctx: Context) -> Details ! db, fail[DbErr], fail[StoreErr]
api.doc:
Evaluates flag `key` straight from the store, reading only that flag, its prerequisites and the
segments they use: cheap enough for every request of a handler that shares the `Db`.
